Net Inward Force and Circular Motion Exercise

The activity describes the quantity as the net inward force required for circular motion.

Correct Physics Idea

For uniform circular motion, the object moves with constant speed but changing direction. The acceleration points toward the center of the circle, so the inward component of the net force causes the motion.

Fnet inward = mv2/r

What Provides the Inward Force?

In this simulation, the ball is attached to a string. The real force pulling the ball inward is the tension in the string.

T = Fnet inward

Important Note

There is no extra force called “centripetal force” added to the free-body diagram. The inward force comes from real forces such as tension, friction, gravity, or normal force, depending on the physical situation.
